blueprint_concepts: Linear combination theorem in a plane
english: Let $\overrightarrow{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{b}$ be two vectors such that $|\overrightarrow{a}|=2$, $|\overrightarrow{b}|=5$ and the angle between $\overrightarrow{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{b}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Let $\overrightarrow{r}$ be a vector coplanar with $\overrightarrow{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{b}$ such that the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{r}$ on $\overrightarrow{a}$ is $11$ and the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{r}$ on $\overrightarrow{b}$ is $13$. Then the value of $|\overrightarrow{r}|^2$ is ______.
hindi: माना $\overrightarrow{a}$ तथा $\overrightarrow{b}$ दो सदिश इस प्रकार हैं कि $|\overrightarrow{a}|=2$, $|\overrightarrow{b}|=5$ है तथा $\overrightarrow{a}$ और $\overrightarrow{b}$ के बीच का कोण $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ है। माना $\overrightarrow{r}$, $\overrightarrow{a}$ तथा $\overrightarrow{b}$ के साथ समतलीय एक सदिश है जिसका $\overrightarrow{a}$ पर अदिश प्रक्षेप $11$ तथा $\overrightarrow{b}$ पर अदिश प्रक्षेप $13$ है। तब $|\overrightarrow{r}|^2$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: The angle between $\overrightarrow{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{b}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, so they are non-zero and non-collinear. By the linear combination theorem in a plane, every vector coplanar with them is $\overrightarrow{r}=x\overrightarrow{a}+y\overrightarrow{b}$ for unique real $x$, $y$.

The scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{r}$ on $\overrightarrow{a}$ is $\dfrac{\overrightarrow{r}\cdot\overrightarrow{a}}{|\overrightarrow{a}|}=11$, so $\overrightarrow{r}\cdot\overrightarrow{a}=22$; similarly $\overrightarrow{r}\cdot\overrightarrow{b}=13\cdot5=65$.
originality_note: New: the vectors a and b are given only through lengths and the angle (no components), and r is fixed by its two scalar projections; the coefficients come from a 2x2 Gram system and |r|^2 = x (r.a) + y (r.b) (way 5). Closest known: 'vector in the plane of a and b whose projection on c is given' (published JEE problems, with components). Different because: there are no components, and both projections are on the spanning vectors themselves.

concept_use.Application of dot product: Scalar projections r.a/|a| and r.b/|b|, a.b = |a||b|cos(pi/3) and |r|^2 = r.r.
concept_use.Linear combination theorem in a plane: r coplanar with the non-collinear a, b is written uniquely as x a + y b, and x, y are found.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, vector and point is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Said 'scalar projection' to avoid the vector-projection reading; coplanarity with two non-collinear vectors makes x, y unique. Changed: replaced 'projection' by 'scalar projection'.
key_step: Writing r = x a + y b and solving the two projection equations.
justification: Routine chain: projections to dot products, a 2x2 linear system, then a magnitude. No insight; Level 2 like 2026-P2-Q1 (L2).
